counterargument.text: The company may have awarded renewable projects that are not disclosed in the integrated report, meaning the apparent lack of gap could be due to incomplete reporting rather than execution risk.

falsification: A capacity-gap claim would be overturned by original records showing that the same projects achieved the required commissioning milestone by the last valid scheduled deadline, after accounting for revisions. Awards not yet due do not establish a shortfall.
proposed_headline: Coal India reports commissioning of a 100 MW Patan solar project but provides no disclosed capacity for awarded renewable projects
proposed_summary: The FY 2025‑26 Integrated Annual Report confirms that Coal India Limited commissioned a 100 MW solar power project at Patan. The report does not list any other renewable projects by status (awarded, under construction, or planned), and no subsequent quarterly filings are available in the supplied sources. Consequently, the hypothesis that a material gap exists between announced renewable capacity and commissioned capacity cannot be confirmed nor refuted with the current evidence.

These systems enhance miner safety by enabling the early detection of hazardous gas concentrations and facilitating timely preventive action. A network of 164 Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Systems (CAAQMS) enables real time monitoring of key air quality parameters, including PM2.5, PM10, SOx, NOx and CO. Strategically installed across mine lease areas, coal handling facilities and surrounding communities, these systems provide continuous environmental surveillance. The monitoring data is seamlessly integrated with the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and respective State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs), ensuring regulatory compliance, transparency and timely environmental oversight. Advanced environmental tele monitoring systems and gas chromatographs are deployed for detailed chemical and gaseous analyses, particularly in underground mines and operational workshops. These technologies facilitate the detection of complex air pollutants, support continuous environmental profiling, and enable timely identification of potential environmental and occupational health risks. Meteorological parameters such as wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rainfall and temperature are monitored alongside air quality indicators to provide a comprehensive understanding of environmental conditions. This integrated approach supports predictive dust dispersion modelling, enables proactive risk assessment and facilitates the effective deployment of dust control and mitigation systems. Noise levels are monitored in decibels using both portable and fixed location monitoring devices during daytime and night time periods. The resulting data supports the implementation of noise control measures, helps maintain compliance with prescribed standards, and informs the development of green belts and buffer zones around sensitive receptors such as schools, hospitals and residential communities. Personal Dust Samplers (PDS) are deployed across critical work areas to monitor employee exposure to airborne particulates.
